question.text: A particle of mass m is released from height h on a smooth curved surface which ends into a vertical loop of radius r, as shown. If h=2r, then

options.text: the particle reaches the top of the loop with zero velocity
the particle reaches the top of the loop with a non-zero velocity
the particle breaks off at a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi></math> from base
the particle breaks off at a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mi>h</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi></math>

solution.text:
To reach the top of loop, particle must have a minimum speed of v=5gr at the bottom of the loop.

but v2=2gh=4gr , so the block won't reach the highest point of the track.
